newsitem.title: CHINA: HKMA's Yam says unworried about attacks on HK dlr.
newsitem.headline: HKMA's Yam says unworried about attacks on HK dlr.

text.p: Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) chief executive Joseph Yam said on Monday he was not concerned about the possibility of speculative attacks on the Hong Kong dollar.

Asked by reporters if he had any concerns that the Hong Kong dollar might be a target of speculators after recent attacks on the Thai baht and the Philippine peso, Yam said he was "absolutely not concerned at all".
Yam said there had been no speculation against the Hong Kong dollar, noting "the exchange rate has been very, very stable".

"And also if you look at our interest rates, they are actually at the same level as U.S. interest rates, which is a very, very good indication that there has been no speculative activity or signficant flow of funds in or out of our currency," Yam said.
Authorities in Thailand and in the Philippines recently have decided to allow their currencies to float more freely following sustained attacks against the baht and the peso.
The Hong Kong dollar is pegged to the U.S. dollar at a rate of HK$7.80.
Yam said that while currencies depended on robust monetary systems, basic economic fundamentals were more important.
"Those basic economic fundamentals support a stable currency and that's what you're seeing in Hong Kong," Yam said.
Yam was speaking to reporters after delivering an address at a debt markets conference in Hong Kong.

The central bank chief also said that he believed bilateral repurchase pacts entered into by many countries in the region have been useful. The pacts are designed to maintain currency stability in disorderly markets.
"I think (the pacts have) been useful. You wouldn't know what otherwise would have been the case (if the network of agreements had not been set up)," Yam said.
Yam called for even greater cooperation among central banks.
"I think there is a need for greater cooperation among central banks in the region, helping each other in the maintenance of currency stability as well as in many other things," he said.
Yam said he was referring to developing financial infrastructure, payments systems and securities clearing systems as well as upgrading banking supervision standards.
